request.input:
Two pages of a personal knowledge base about its owner's life. Each page describes one project.

PAGE A
Name: Atlas Migration
Also called: Atlas
About: Atlas Migration moves Northwind Labs' nightly batch pipelines from a legacy cluster to a managed warehouse.
Facts:
- Atlas Migration is owned by Alex
- Atlas moves nightly batch pipelines to a managed warehouse
- Atlas is in the testing phase
- Atlas go-live is planned for 2026-11-15
- Northwind Labs sponsors Atlas
- Part of Alex's work at Northwind Labs

PAGE B
Name: Atlas Reporting
About: Atlas Reporting was a client reporting suite Alex built at Fabrikam Analytics for a retail client.
Facts:
- Alex built Atlas Reporting
- Atlas Reporting is finished
- Part of Alex's work at Fabrikam Analytics
- Atlas Reporting uses Tableau

What the owner's sources say:
- Alex worries the Atlas migration deadline is unrealistic
- Alex has worked at Northwind Labs since February 2023 and became a senior data engineer in March › Alex leads the Atlas Migration, which moves nightly batch pipelines to a managed warehouse
- Planning the Atlas cut-over: dbt models first, then Airflow DAGs
- Alex asked the big model how to sequence the Atlas cut-over.
- Northwind Labs, Porto — Data engineer, then senior data engineer (Feb 2023 – present) › Lead the Atlas Migration of batch pipelines to a managed warehouse.
- Fabrikam Analytics, Lisbon — Analytics engineer (Jun 2019 – Jan 2023) › Built client reporting dashboards, including Atlas Reporting for a retail client (2021–2022), in Tableau.

questions.name: same
questions.instructions: Are page A and page B about the same project?

choices.description: yes, one project: one name is another way of writing the other (a nickname, a misspelling, an abbreviation, a translation, a longer form)
no, two different projects that only look alike or are related
